summary_en: Fiscal 2027 interim dividend of 36 yen per share (up 2 yen) and full-year dividend of 70 yen per share (up 2 yen), reflecting upward revision of net income forecast driven by higher interest income following Bank of Japan policy rate increases; payout ratio 40.0%.
title_en: Notice Regarding Revision of Full-Year Earnings Forecast for Fiscal Year Ended March 31, 2027 and Revision (Increase) of Year-End Dividend Forecast
translation_en_brief:
The San-in Godo Bank revised its fiscal 2027 earnings forecast upward on November 12, 2026, and increased its dividend accordingly. The parent company's net income attributable to shareholders of the parent is now projected at 194.8 billion yen, an increase of 23.6 billion yen (13.7%) from the previous forecast of 171.2 billion yen. Earnings per share is expected to reach 172.68 yen, up from 166.34 yen.

The upward revision reflects stronger interest income driven by the Bank of Japan's policy rate increases. The bank's interest income and securities dividend income are expected to exceed previous estimates as a result of the higher rate environment.

In line with the earnings revision, the bank increased its full-year dividend per share to 70 yen from the previously announced 68 yen. The year-end dividend is raised to 36 yen per share (interim dividend remains 34 yen). This represents a 2-yen increase from the prior forecast of 68 yen full-year dividend. The payout ratio on a consolidated basis is projected at 40.0%, consistent with the bank's dividend policy targeting a 40% payout ratio.
